title: Kepler to Müller, 22 April 1630
author: Johannes Kepler
source: Johannes Kepler's letter to Philipp Müller written at Sagan on 22 April 1630, on his return from Wallenstein at Gitschin, sending 600 copies of the *Ephemerides* for 1630–1633, with notes on type and astronomical signs, and asking Müller to urge Jacob Bartsch and his wife Susanna to come to the christening of Kepler's newborn daughter. The original is lost; the copy is in the Bibliothèque nationale, Paris (Nouv. acq. lat. 1635, fol. 99; 89, 8. P). First printed in *Nova Kepleriana* 4, ed. Walther von Dyck and Max Caspar, Abhandlungen der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Math.-naturw. Abteilung 31, no. 1 (Munich, 1927), 74–76.
transcribed_from: the page images of the 1927 printing.
summary: Back from Wallenstein at Gitschin, Kepler sends 600 copies of the *Ephemerides* for 1630–1633, comments on the type and the signs cast for them, and asks Müller to urge Bartsch and Susanna to hurry to Sagan for the christening of his newborn daughter.

notes.note: Kepler's Latin translation of Plutarch's *De facie in orbe lunae*, published with his *Somnium* in 1634.
The *Somnium*, Kepler's “lunar astronomy”, a dream of a journey to the moon, with his notes; it was published in 1634.
